messages.text:
Hi,

HashWatcher is showing the hashrate straight from my BS-4's /api/system/info, and it does not scale or filter chips. At 650 MHz, smallCoreCount 7000, and asicCount 4, that config should be about 18.2 TH/s, but hashRate and the 1-minute, 10-minute, and 1-hour averages all sit at 9.83–9.88 TH/s while the board is still drawing 262 W at 11.69 V and 22.4 A. Can you confirm whether v1.0.38-alpha4 is under-reporting hashrate, or whether only about half the BM1373 domains are actually returning work on a unit that still enumerates 4 chips?

Also, will there be support to install HarloOS onto a BitAxe Gamma Turbo/GT 801?

Thank you,
Scott
Searched the web · Bitfortun BS-4 BM1373 firmware v1.0.38 hashrate
Searched the web · harlolabs Harlo OS supported miners
Handed to the team · I can't confirm the BS-4 stock firmware's hashrate accounting from public source

Hi Scott,

Short answer: I can't confirm either one from the numbers alone. But your readings point more toward a counting problem than toward chips that have stopped working. Here's why, and the test that will settle it.

Your expected figure is right. 650 MHz x 7,000 small cores x 4 chips comes to 18.2 TH/s, which matches the BS-4's
4.5 TH out of each one
. You're getting about 54% of that. The power is the giveaway: 262 W at 9.85 TH/s is about 26.6 J/TH, roughly double what BM1373 chips use at that clock. If half the domains had really stopped hashing, the draw should have dropped well below 262 W. So all four chips look like they're doing full work.

That leaves two possibilities. Either v1.0.38-alpha4 counts the hashrate wrong, or the chips are hashing and the firmware is losing about half the results before they reach the pool. Both point to firmware rather than the board. Your 1-minute, 10-minute and 1-hour averages all agree, so this is a steady ratio, not share luck.

I can't check the code to see which it is. Bitfortun has published the BS-1 firmware, but the BS-4 source isn't out. Someone has an open request on their GitHub
for the complete source for the firmware version shipped on the BS-4
. One related clue: the developers who added support for the 4-chip BM1373 Nexus S1 to their own firmware weren't sure which hash counter register the chip uses,
0x90 (used here, and the per-chip rates look right) or 0x8C as in bitaxe
. A wrong register or scale factor would give exactly the kind of steady ratio you're seeing. That's my hypothesis, not a confirmed finding.

The test that decides it is the pool's number, because the pool doesn't rely on the miner's own figure. Let the unit run for at least two hours, then take the pool's hashrate, or work it out yourself: total accepted share difficulty x 2^32 / elapsed seconds. With a few thousand shares the error is a couple of percent, so 18 versus 9.8 will be obvious.

If the pool sees about 18 TH/s, the firmware is under-reporting and your unit is fine. If the pool also sees about 9.8 TH/s, the work really is being lost. In that case, please send the per-chip or per-domain section of the JSON if your build has one (newer ESP-Miner-based builds call it hashrateMonitor), along with sharesAccepted, sharesRejected and any error percentage field.

A second check is to run Harlo OS, our own free firmware, which lists the Bitfortun BS4 as supported. With Harlo OS
the miner stops grading its own homework
 and takes the
hash from the shares your pool accepts
. I couldn't check the current version from here, so get the latest build from harlolabs.com. You
flash from your browser
 in Chrome or Edge, and HashWatcher
keeps working after you flash
.

On the Bitaxe Gamma Turbo / GT 801: it isn't on the current list of 17 supported models. The only Bitaxe entries are the Gamma 601 and the Naja Duo. The page says
more added most weeks. Not on the list yet means not yet, not never.
 I can't give you a date for the GT 801.

I've sent both questions and all your numbers to JD, our hardware lead, who also builds Harlo OS. He'll pick them up tomorrow at 10am ET and you'll get the answer by email. For a faster answer, post the JSON and the pool numbers on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and tag @nullhashrate. JD and the community are very active there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
